# AI Migrations

> Lessons from products migrated to another language or framework with AI, for anyone running a
> large project with AI agents.

**Unofficial. No company named here endorses or is affiliated with this project.** Company and
product names describe the subject of each case only. Summaries are in our own words and link to
their primary sources.

## What it does

<!-- contents: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Now: 13 cases (Slack, Zalando, Airbnb, Google, Spotify, Uber, 1Password, Bun, Asana, Intel, Shopify, GitHub, Bloomberg), 137 lessons on 16 aspect pages, and a checklist of 12 questions.
<!-- /contents -->

- **Cases** ([cases/](cases/)): one file per migration done with AI, from engineering posts,
  papers and official repositories. Each says what AI did, what rule-based tools and people did,
  how the result was checked, the numbers with their basis, and what went wrong, including what
  the source leaves out.
- **Lessons** ([lessons/](lessons/)): what the cases teach about large AI-driven work, by aspect
  (reviews, tests, orchestration, rollout, cost). The sources stay migrations; the lessons apply
  more widely.
- **Checklist** ([checklist.md](checklist.md)): questions a coding agent can measure on a
  repository before a migration, each with a check and the evidence behind it.
- **Pitfalls** ([pitfalls.md](pitfalls.md)): what the old stack does without being asked, by kind
  of move, and seams for moving in steps.
- **For agents** ([llms.txt](llms.txt)): one line per case and lesson page, so an agent reads
  only what it needs.

[index.md](index.md) lists everything. [log.md](log.md) records what each update covered.

## Try it

Open your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) in the project you are thinking of
migrating. Step 1 only reads your project; steps 2 and 3 are optional.

### Step 1: review

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow it. Run the checklist on this project: measure every question with its check; do not judge from memory. Report in the checklist's report format: each answer with its evidence and the cases behind it, then a go or no-go with the main risks. Change nothing.
```

What to change, if anything, is your call.

### Step 2: apply

```text
Apply the proposals you marked "do" (or: apply proposals 1, 3 and 5). For each, first state the check that proves it, then make the change and run that check. Write the record the checklist defines in docs/migration-review.md: every proposal with its status, the event that shows it and the date. Name the newest log.md entry this review covered.
```

### Step 3: revisit, and tell us what happened

When the code has moved on, or the migration has started, paste:

```text
Read docs/migration-review.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/log.md. Re-run only the open, waiting and stopped-holding items, and any question whose measurement may have moved or that a newer log entry changed. Update the record. Then draft a field report as https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md describes, and show it to me before posting.
```

A [field report](docs/field-reports.md) says which questions foresaw the problems you hit and
which missed them; it is how the checklist improves.

### Not migrating? Tips for any large AI project

Many lessons describe how AI agents behave on large work, not only in migrations. Those tagged
"Old system as oracle: no" carry over as they are. To compare them with how your project works:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow its route for large AI-driven work that is not a migration. Use only lessons tagged "Old system as oracle: no", or "partly" where this project already has a substitute check. Compare them with how this project's agents and sessions work today. Change nothing: give numbered proposals, each with the lesson ID, what the project does now, the change, its cost, and the check that would prove it.
```

## Contributing

Corrections are welcome: a wrong number, a broken link, a summary that misreads its source. Open
an issue; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) describes the case
format and the rules every file follows.
